what: One fresh session (claude-opus-5-5, effort medium) read eight files with one plain Read each, in parallel; for each, whether the first Read returned every line. g = concatenated real design/ + build/ texts; p = real process3 prose (process4_disposition.md + process4_counterarguments.md, table-dense).
earlier_probe: A 96,000-byte concatenation of design/ + build/ came back cut after line 516 (69,864 bytes). The tool result itself carried no cut notice; the session noticed and read the rest with an offset Read.
note: The cut is set by tokens (about 25,000), not bytes: real governing prose reads whole to at least 76,000 bytes; table-dense prose is cut between 63,381 and 67,409 bytes. When a file is cut, the part returned is well short of the cap (53-70 KB here).
